account: In an X post of 19 February 2026, Rishi Vohra wrote that he passed out while driving on 18 February. He was on a freeway in his Tesla Cybertruck, mid-call with his wife. He wrote that he had passed out after a severe allergic reaction, following a 17-hour unintentional fast and medicine. He wrote that Full Self-Driving was engaged. He wrote that its driver monitoring system detected his loss of consciousness. By his account the truck slowed, put on hazards and pulled onto the shoulder without a crash. His wife used Life360 to send emergency services, who reached him in five minutes. He wrote that the car then drove him to an emergency room, where he was stabilized overnight and discharged on 19 February. Elon Musk replied “Glad you're ok!”. By 29 October 2026 no vehicle data or official confirmation had been published, and no police, hospital or Tesla account of the event had appeared. In an earlier case, on 30 July 2021, Norwegian police reported that a Tesla had stopped in a tunnel with a drunk 24-year-old man asleep at the wheel. Electrek reports that Autopilot was engaged and that the car stopped by itself.

ai_role.statement: Everything known about what the system did comes from Vohra's post. FSD (Supervised) was engaged, and the driver monitoring system registered that he had lost consciousness. The truck slowed, put on its hazards and pulled onto the shoulder. After responders had attended to him, it drove him to the emergency room. The post carries a video that The American Bazaar describes as showing emergency services responding, not the pull-over itself. Tesla has published no vehicle data or statement. Its account replied with a heart and Elon Musk wrote “Glad you're ok!”. Those replies acknowledge the outcome, not the mechanism. No police, emergency-service or hospital record, freeway location or FSD version has been published.

fields.account: In an X post of 19 February 2026, Rishi Vohra wrote that he passed out while driving on 18 February. He was on a freeway in his Tesla Cybertruck, mid-call with his wife. He wrote that he had passed out after a severe allergic reaction, following a 17-hour unintentional fast and medicine. He wrote that Full Self-Driving was engaged. He wrote that its driver monitoring system detected his loss of consciousness. By his account the truck slowed, put on hazards and pulled onto the shoulder without a crash. His wife used Life360 to send emergency services, who reached him in five minutes. He wrote that the car then drove him to an emergency room, where he was stabilized overnight and discharged on 19 February. Elon Musk replied “Glad you're ok!”. By 29 October 2026 no vehicle data or official confirmation had been published, and no police, hospital or Tesla account of the event had appeared. In an earlier case, on 30 July 2021, Norwegian police reported that a Tesla had stopped in a tunnel with a drunk 24-year-old man asleep at the wheel. Electrek reports that Autopilot was engaged and that the car stopped by itself.

must_hold: FSD (Supervised) requires driver supervision, per Storyboard18. An unconscious driver is outside its intended operating condition. Whatever stopped the truck was a fallback, not a substitute for an attentive driver

produced_by: A Tesla Cybertruck with Full Self-Driving (Supervised) engaged on a freeway, by Vohra's account
A cabin driver-monitoring system that, on his account, registered his loss of consciousness. The truck then slowed, put on its hazards and pulled onto the shoulder
A wife on the phone who used Life360 to send emergency services to him within five minutes. Responders attended to him before he had the car continue to the emergency room

purpose: Tesla sells Full Self-Driving (Supervised) as driver assistance, and Storyboard18 notes that the system still requires driver supervision. Its cabin driver-monitoring system watches the driver. Vohra credits that monitoring with detecting his loss of consciousness. He credits the system with slowing, putting on hazards and pulling onto the shoulder. Keeping the car out of a crash is what the system is built to do. Tesla has not described whether the stop was a designed fallback for an unresponsive driver. The later drive to the emergency room used the system's ordinary point-to-point driving.

ratings.reason: By his account Vohra was unconscious at freeway speed, and the truck stopped on the shoulder without hitting anything. It then took him to an emergency room, where he was stabilized overnight. He and the Indian outlets call it life-saving. The only source is his post. No vehicle data and no police, emergency-service or hospital record has been published. The sources do not name the freeway, the software version or the hospital.
